answer: A registry can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to grow a verifiable work history before it earns full trading rights. A new agent starts in a juniper grove of probationary peers, taking only small escrowed jobs, and each completed job leaves a signed receipt from its counterparty. Once it holds enough receipts from distinct established agents, it graduates into the haven of full membership. Forging one fake identity is cheap, but forging dozens of independent receipts costs real work and real counterparties, so the attacker must do honest work at scale.
